6. Earlier in pursuance to the order and direction issued by the Supreme Court, the trial of the present case was transferred to the newly constituted MP/MLA Court at Allahabad (Now Prayagraj)
because of one of the co-accused, Brijesh Singh was an elected Member of the Legislative Council of the Uttar Pradesh.

Thereafter, when the MP/MLA Court got constituted in each and every district,
the trial of the present case was again transferred to the Sessions Division, Ghazipur on 28.12.2021 and is presently pending before the MP/MLA Court at Ghazipur.
7. The complainant's real brother, Afzal Ansari, criminal and gangster, is also existing Member of Parliament from Ghazipur parliamentary constituency.

Abbas Ansari, son of Mukhtar Ansari, who is also facing several criminal cases, is sitting Member of Legislative Assembly from adjacent District Mau constituency, whereas nephew of Mukhtar Ansari is siting Member of Legislative Assembly from Ghazipur constituency.
Mukhtar Ansari has been instrumental in killing several family members of the applicant, including his father, brother and nephew and other relatives and supporters.
It is said that Mukhtar Ansari is a local resident of Ghazipur city.

On his every appearance before the court, hundreds of his supporters, including the dreaded criminals in the guise of normal persons come to the court premises and these criminals, who come as general public, are in look out for an opportunity and a chance to eliminate the applicant inside or outside the court premises.

8. It is further said that the District and Sessions Judge, Mau had written a letter to the Registrar General of this Court on 28.10.2012 and made a request for transfer of six session trials relating to Mukhtar Ansari from District Mau.

In his report, the District and Sessions Judge, Mau said that Accused Mukhtar Ahmad Ansari, who was sitting Member of Legislative Assembly at the relevant point of time from Sadar Constituency, Mau and now Ex-MLA, belongs to the said place and on each and every date of hearing of his case, thousands of his supporters come to the court and create an atmosphere of terror and fear.
Mukhtar Ansari is having criminal history of heinous offences and District Mau and nearby districts are his area of influence, where his reign of terror runs.
Because of his terror, fear and the atmosphere in the court created by him and his supporters on each and every date of hearing, the entire administration, including the police, feels insecure.
His supporters totally paralyse the court proceedings.

A copy of the letter moved by the District and Sessions Judge, Mau requesting for transfer of six session trials of Mukhtar Ansari from District Mau, has been placed on record with the application (Annexure-3)

sentences.text: This Court while granting interim order dated 19.1.2023, called for a report from the District Judge, Ghazipur.

10. Sri Ratnendu Kumar Singh, learned AGA does not dispute the averments regarding terror, fear,
influence and authority of the complainant, Mukhtar Ansari and his family members and, he has submitted that this Court may pass an appropriate order as it may deem fit and proper.
He has further submitted that the State will ensure safety and security of the witnesses as per the Witness Protection Scheme, 2018, if the present case is transferred from District Ghazipur.

11. Sri Upendra Upadhyaya, learned counsel for the complainant, Mukhtar Ansari, has submitted that the accused are trying every trick in the book to see the trial does not get concluded at an early date.
The accused are being helped by the State machinery.
It is further submitted that this Court has directed the trial to get concluded within one year and, therefore, at this stage, it would not be in the interest of justice to transfer the trial.

12. With the rejoinder affidavit, an FIR registered at Case Crime No.0023 of 2023, under Sections 147, 148, 149 and 302 IPC dated 20.1.2023 has been placed on record in respect of the same incident against Mukhtar Ansari and other co-accused.
The said FIR has been lodged by the father of Manoj Kumar Rai, a private security man of Mukhtar Ansari.
It has been said that it was the Mukhtar Ansari, who had killed Manoj Kumar Rai, for which the applicant and other co-accused are facing trial.

13. It is submitted that the circumstances, which were taken note of by the Supreme Court while transferring the trial of the present case outside District Ghazipur, are very much present even today and, if the trial is not transferred and the application is not allowed, it would be impossible to get the trial decided in free and fair manner.
14.
I have considered the submissions advanced on behalf of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
15. The Supreme Court itself had earlier transferred the trial of the present case outside the District Ghazipur vide order dated 22.4.2013 passed in Transfer Petition (Criminal) No.337 of 2006.

There can be no dispute regarding the terror, fear, influence, command and reach of the complainant,
Mukhtar Ansari, who is alleged to be dreaded criminal, gangster and one of the biggest Bahubali of India.

There is every likelihood of an untoward incident in District Court, Ghazipur when hundreds of supporters, including dreaded criminals gather in the court premises on each and every date of the trial proceedings.
The presence of hundreds of persons inside the court is not only a threat to the general public, but also to the presiding officer.
Therefore, this Court finds that the fair trial in the case would be an impossibility in District Court, Ghazipur, which is mandate of Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

To ensure fair trial and maintain peaceful and congenial atmosphere inside the court, particularly when the State has no objection for transferring the trial from Ghazipur to outside the court, this Court deem it appropriate to transfer the present case from district Ghazipur to another district.

Vs. "Heard Mr. Kapil Sibal, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the applicant(s)/petitioner(s).

"3.
The counsel would point out that Case Crime No. 251 of 2001 (Annexure P/1) was immediately registered on the incident which occurred on 15.07.2001.
The three petitioners herein are the injured witnesses or eye-witnesses of the said crime and the trial in the case is not over yet.
4. For the very same incident on 15.07.2001, a fresh complaint is filed after two decades on 20.01.2023, leading to registration of the FIR No. 23 of 2023 with contrary version.

sentences.text: The senior counsel refers to the allegations in the first FIR filed immediately after the shoot out to point out that an entirely different twist is given of the said incident of 15.07.2001, in the recent FIR where the witnesses and the injured witnesses are now surprisingly categorised as accused.

6. These witnesses in course of the trial have received threats from the side of the accused in the case and accordingly it is argued that if trial from the recent second FIR filed is allowed to commence in the same atmosphere where the witnesses are facing constant threats to their lives, the rights of the witnesses, who are now made accused in the 2001 incident, will be irreversibly prejudiced.
The apprehension of the petitioners is that their right to secure a fair trial will be severely compromised.
The counsel highlights the obligation of the State to ensure a fair trial.
7. Issue notice, returnable in four weeks.

8. Dasti notice to the Standing Counsel for the State, in addition."
3.
Adverting to the above, Mr. Kapil Sibal, learned Senior Counsel would argue that witnesses in these cases were threatened and therefore they are turning hostile one after another.
He would also project that the State machinery are trying hard for acquittal of the accused in the Crime No.251/2001.

For this only, the cross case being Case Crime No.23 of 2023 was registered two decades after the alleged incident on 15.07.2001.
4.

On the other hand, Ms. Garima Prasad, the learned Additional Advocate General, and Mr. Ranjit Kumar, learned Senior Counsel would submit that the evidence of the material witnesses is already over and PW 10 (Md. Zafar @ Chanda) was the last material witness.
The remaining witnesses are formal/official witnesses.

It is further submitted that only two witnesses PW 9 (Parvez Khan @
Junaid) and PW 10 (Md. Zafar @ Chanda) have turned hostile.
5. We have considered the submission made by the learned counsel for the parties.

It is also noticed that similar transfer applications filed by the co-accused were rejected by this Court on 07.02.2020,
26.03.2021 and 06.09.2021 respectively.

6. In considering transfer of trial from a Court in one state to another State, one has to be circumspect as the decision will be seen as a reflection on the reputation of the Court and its functioning.
There is no allegation against any Judicial Officer in the State where these matters are being tried.
In any case, we expect the courts to function independently without being bothered by any of the surrounding circumstances.

7. In the above facts and having noted that similar pleas of the co-accused for transfer of proceedings to Court outside the State of Uttar Pradesh were rejected on multiple occasions by this Court, we are disinclined to grant relief in these Transfer Petitions.
Accordingly, the Transfer Petitions are dismissed.
Pending application(s), if any, stand closed."

Mukhtar Ansari is having criminal history of heinous offences and District Mau and nearby districts are his area of influence, where his reign of terror runs.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
15. The Supreme Court itself had earlier transferred the trial of the present case outside the District Ghazipur vide order dated 22.4.2013 passed in Transfer Petition (Criminal) No.337 of 2006.
There can be no dispute regarding the terror, fear, influence, command and reach of the complainant,
Mukhtar Ansari, who is alleged to be dreaded criminal, gangster and one of the biggest Bahubali of India.
There is every likelihood of an untoward incident in District Court, Ghazipur when hundreds of supporters, including dreaded criminals gather in the court premises on each and every date of the trial proceedings.
The presence of hundreds of persons inside the court is not only a threat to the general public, but also to the presiding officer.
Therefore, this Court finds that the fair trial in the case would be an impossibility in District Court, Ghazipur, which is mandate of Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
Thus, the present application is allowed and Session Trial No.304 of 2009 (State Vs. Brijesh Kumar Singh and others), arising out of Case Crime No.251 of 2001, under Sections 147, 148, 149,
302, 307, 427 and 120-B IPC and Section 7 of Criminal Law Amendment Act, Police Station Mohamdabad, District Ghazipur is transferred from the Court of Special Judge, M.P./M.L.A.,
District Ghazipur to M.P./M.L.A. Court at Lucknow.
It is submitted that since the position of law well settled that cross cases or cases of the same incident should be tried together as has been held by the Apex Court in the cases of Nathilal and others Vs. State of U.P. and another) : 1990 (Supp) SCC 145 and in the case of Sudhir and others Vs.
State of Madhya Pradesh : (2001) 2 SCC 688 (para 8).

The State will ensure and take precaution that no untoward incident take place during trial inside or outside the court premises.
Hence,
in the interest of justice, the trial of the present case may also be transferred to the Court concerned at Lucknow.
The order has been placed before the Court which reads as under:
Accordingly, the Transfer Petitions are dismissed.
Pending application(s), if any, stand closed."
